close_reason: Landed in 1491170 alongside JMAP-t307.10. Option (a) per bead: rustdoc + README contract. part_to_jmap rustdoc adds a 'blob_id_for contract' section spelling out the idempotence requirement and the per-leaf call frequency. message_to_jmap_body rustdoc has its own 'blob_id_for contract' section explaining the per-appearance frequency (up to 3x for a plain-only leaf). README's part_to_jmap section adds a bolded 'MUST be idempotent on part.part_id' line, and a Gotchas bullet documents the multi-invocation call frequency.
description:
The blob_id_for closure passed to message_to_jmap_body (src/lib.rs:127)
and part_to_jmap (src/lib.rs:73) is invoked multiple times for the same
leaf ParsedPart, but the contract on the closure is silent about
idempotence.

Trace of message_to_jmap_body:
  1. part_to_jmap_inner walks the full body_structure tree — one
     blob_id_for(part) call per non-multipart leaf.
  2. text_body.iter() re-walks each text leaf via find_by_id and
     part_to_jmap_inner — another blob_id_for(part) call per text leaf.
  3. html_body.iter() — another call per html leaf.
  4. attachments.iter() — another call per attachment leaf.

For a plain-text-only message — by far the most common email shape —
the single text/plain leaf gets the closure called THREE times because
html_body mirrors text_body per RFC 8621 §4.1.4. The existing test
message_to_jmap_body_plain_text_body (src/lib.rs:296-309) confirms
both lists have length 1 for plain-only input.

What goes wrong for the caller: a storage-backend author writing a
counter-based or remote-allocate blob_id_for closure (the natural
inclination — \"give me a fresh blob ID for this part\") will get
DIFFERENT blob IDs for the same logical leaf in body_structure,
text_body, and html_body. The JMAP Email/get wire response then has
the same partId surfaced under multiple distinct blobIds, breaking
client expectations. There is no error signal — the wire format is
syntactically valid, just internally inconsistent.

The newly-rewritten README \"How it works\" section (README.md:111-125)
documents the closure pattern but says nothing about idempotence. The
new example (examples/parse_eml.rs:36) and bench (benches/mime_pipeline.rs:299)
both use Id::from(format!(\"blob-{}\", part.part_id)) — idempotent by
virtue of being a pure function of part_id — but neither flags the
requirement. A consumer copy-pasting the example pattern who then
substitutes a counter has no way to know they have introduced a bug.

The maintainer's own tests pass because they use the idempotent
pattern; downstream consumers integrating with real blob stores using
their natural blob-ID assignment patterns will hit the wire-format
defect with no warning from this crate.

Fix options (maintainer's choice):
  (a) Rustdoc + README contract: state explicitly that blob_id_for
      MUST return the same Id for repeated calls on the same part,
      AND document the call frequency (once per appearance, not once
      per unique leaf). This puts the burden on the caller but is the
      minimal-impact fix.
  (b) Implementation change: memoize closure results inside
      message_to_jmap_body keyed by part_id (or by &ParsedPart pointer
      identity) so the closure is invoked once per unique leaf
      regardless of how many body lists reference it. This silently
      fixes non-idempotent callers and matches what callers will
      assume from \"once per leaf\" framing.

Workspace context: PLAN.md item 6 (\"body_value_part_ids disjointness
is not asserted\", lines 174-178) gestures at the related disjointness
question but mis-classifies it — RFC 8621 §4.1.4 mandates that
html_body mirrors text_body for plain-only messages, so the lists
are NOT disjoint by design.
title: blob_id_for closure called multiple times per leaf; idempotence undocumented
